name: Menthol
short: Case reports: fatal workplace menthol poisoning; skin and muscle necrosis, kidney inflammation after topical methyl salicylate-menthol then a heating pad. Also skin irritation; mouth, lip allergy.
text: Serious harms appear in case reports: a fatal menthol poisoning was reported in a worker accidentally exposed in a peppermint factory, and one patient developed full-thickness skin and muscle necrosis and persistent interstitial nephritis after applying a methyl salicylate and menthol product followed by a heating pad. In phase I patch studies in healthy volunteers, a 1% diclofenac plus 3% menthol gel caused minimal redness, glazing and peeling in 77% of participants during repeated application, with similar patterns for a menthol-only gel (the abstract does not give its strength); one participant showed possible sensitisation to the combination gel, its irritation and sensitisation potential was greater than that of the reference treatments, and no treatment-related adverse events were reported. Contact allergy is described in case reports and a case series: 12 patients with mouth symptoms (burning mouth, recurrent ulcers or lichenoid reactions) had contact sensitivity to menthol and/or peppermint, and 6 of the 9 who could be followed improved after avoiding them; another report describes allergic lip inflammation from menthol in toothpaste and throat medicine. A case report describes asthma in a 40-year-old woman exposed to mentholated toothpaste and sweets, confirmed by bronchial challenge. A cosmetic safety assessment noted evidence that menthol can enhance skin penetration of other agents. No drug interaction data were found in the cited sources.
